name: Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp

criteria.description: Presence of painful, fluctuant nodules and abscesses on the scalp
Development of interconnected sinus tracts with purulent discharge
Progressive scarring alopecia with hair loss in affected areas
Histopathological evidence of follicular destruction with neutrophilic and granulomatous inflammation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of painful scalp nodules with sinus tract formation and scarring alopecia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; no universally accepted formal criteria exist.

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) during active disease
Bacterial cultures from purulent discharge may show Staphylococcus aureus or mixed flora
imaging: Ultrasound showing fluid collections and sinus tracts in scalp tissue
MRI may demonstrate extent of soft tissue involvement and exclude osteomyelitis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible association with follicular occlusion tetrad
other: Histopathology reveals follicular destruction, neutrophilic abscesses, granulomatous inflammation, and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily affects apocrine gland-bearing areas (axillae, groin) rather than scalp
Typical double comedones and recurrent abscesses in intertriginous zones
Fungal infection with scaling, broken hairs, and black dots
Usually lacks sinus tract formation and scarring alopecia initially
Chronic neutrophilic inflammation with tufted hair follicle openings
Scarring alopecia but typically less purulent discharge

redFlags: Signs of underlying osteomyelitis or deep tissue infection
Systemic symptoms such as high fever or malaise indicating severe infection
references: Frew JW, et al. Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp: a review. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019;81(6):1447-1455.
Orphanet: Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp - ORPHA345
